consensus_summary: Tares symbolize the sons of the evil one (false/counterfeit believers) sown by the devil among the sons of the kingdom (wheat); they coexist until the end-of-age harvest when angels separate and burn them. Core fixed by Jesus’ own interpretation.
book_summary: The counterfeit sown among the wheat by the enemy—a weed that mimics true grain until harvest, then bound in bundles and burned; the children of the wicked one, distinct from the winnowed chaff.
consensus_core_identification: sons of the evil one / false or counterfeit believers mixed with the righteous
book_core_identification: the counterfeit / children of the wicked one sown among the wheat
boundary_disagreement: None material; book’s added note distinguishing tares from winnowed chaff merely separates two parallel biblical images without redefining the tares’ referent or cases.
rationale: Both cores rest on the identical Matthean identification (tares = children of the wicked one). Book language is a direct, compact paraphrase of the settled consensus primary meaning; botanical mimicry, enemy-sowing, and final burning are already standard. The chaff distinction is an immaterial clarification, not a boundary shift or replacement of referent.
strongest_objection: The explicit ‘distinct from winnowed chaff’ clause could be read as an extra restriction, yet it does not exclude any cases the consensus assigns to tares themselves.
